name: Data Science
publishedCredits: 54 points in the CS bulletin’s category totals; 18 courses on the standard mathematics path.
notes: The departments require letter grades above D. The Statistics table includes the accelerated calculus option, the honors mathematics route, and COMS W4130. The current CS quick guide omits W4130, so confirm eligibility and availability before selecting it.
The CS bulletin assigns 15 points to prerequisites, 12 to statistics, 12 to computer science, and 15 to electives. The selected courses’ actual point values can yield a different total.
The introduction requirement accepts STAT UN1001 or UN1101 taken in spring 2018 or earlier in place of STAT UN1201.

groups.label: Linear algebra
groups.note: The Statistics table lists MATH UN2010. The CS department guide also accepts linear algebra offered by Applied Mathematics.

notes: The honors sequence requires placement. The Mathematics Department publishes qualifying AP and IB scores.

groups.label: Computer science electives
groups.note: Includes the published COMS W47xx course family except W4771. W4721 has overlapping content with W4771. Check enrollment restrictions and overlapping-credit rules when selecting machine learning courses.

name: Information Science
publishedCredits: 13 major courses plus Calculus I preparation. Each interdisciplinary elective carries at least 3 points.
notes: Applies to students declaring in fall 2026 or later. The department guide names Calculus I as prerequisite preparation and permits COMS W1007 as the introductory course. Earlier declarations use a different major.
The guide lists CSEE W4119 and CSOR W4231 for networking and algorithms. The College table uses alternate subject or division codes for the same titles.

groups.label: Linear algebra or probability and statistics
Courses in one other department
groups.note: Choose three distinct courses from the same non-CS department, each numbered 3000 or higher and worth at least 3 points. The indexed choices span Economics, Mathematics, Philosophy, Political Science and Statistics. Other departments also qualify. Check eligibility with the host department.

name: Statistics
publishedCredits: 14 courses on the standard mathematics path. The department specifies course counts.
notes: Plan the major with the director of undergraduate studies. All major courses must receive a letter grade above D.

The College table and department planning guidance specify three electives. A conflicting sentence in the same bulletin table says five. The planner follows the 14-course total and the department guidance.

groups.label: Linear regression
groups.note: Students preparing for an actuarial career may substitute GU4282 for GU4205. GU4205 is the standard requirement.

groups.label: At least one Statistics elective
groups.note: One of the three approved electives must be a Statistics Department course numbered 4221–4291.

groups.label: Additional advanced electives
groups.note: Obtain approval for the complete three-course elective plan. Advanced courses in mathematics, statistics, applied mathematics, industrial engineering and operations research, computer science, and quantitative social science may be approved. The department recommends both Modern Analysis courses for students preparing for graduate study.
